newsitem.title: USA: UAL names employee liaison executive.
newsitem.headline: UAL names employee liaison executive.

text.p: UAL Corp, which faces increased tensions with some of its United Airlines employees, said Friday it named a new executive who will act as a liaison between the company and worker groups.
UAL, which has been majority-owned by employees since mid-1994, said it named William Hobgood as senior vice president - people, effective immediately.
He replaces Paul George, a human resources executive who retired recently.

In a statement, UAL Chairman Gerald Greenwald called Hobgood "the right man in the right place at a time when United is accelerating the development of the participatory, post-ESOP culture that has been instrumental in the company's extraordinary turnaround since 1994."
Pilots, machinists and salaried workers at United own a majority of the company as part of an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP).
Despite the ESOP, UAL has seen tensions escalate in recent months with some of its employees.

Last month, members of the Air Line Pilots Association (ALPA) began withdrawing from non-essential task forces at United Airlines as part of a protest of what they called poor relations with management.

The pilots, along with some groups within the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, recently turned down a mid-term pay raise offer from United. That issue now goes to arbitration.

In addition, the Association of Flight Attendants, who do not participate in the ESOP at United, said this week they kicked off their "CHAOS" campaign to protest what they call the slow pace of contract negotiations with United.
Spokesmen for ALPA and the AFA were not immediately available to comment on Hobgood's appointment.

Hobgood had been a private practice attorney specializing in mediation and arbitration. He spent 14 years with the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service, where he was commissioner and later director, mediation services.

He also served as Assistant Secretary of Labor for Labor-Management Relations during the Carter administration. Most recently he was vice president of the Mediation, Research and Education Project at Northwestern University.
